銘.meaning: A champion's <part>gold</part> trophy is too shiny for a sticker, so the jeweller takes a tiny chisel and cuts her <part>name</part> into its side, letter by letter, so deep that a thousand polishings won't rub it away. Those words in the metal are an <kanji>inscription</kanji>.
銘.on: Tiny swirls round the letters make a <sound>ma</sound>ze an ant could get lost in.

幽.meaning: A hermit moves into a <part>mountain</part> where two paths <part>twist</part> in and in, round and round, until no visitor can follow. Postmen give up; even echoes get lost. Alone with a goat, he has found the perfect place to <kanji>seclude</kanji> himself.
幽.on: His only visitor is a <sound>u</sound>nicorn who knows the way.
幽.kun: His pond is so deep that the <sound>fu</sound>ll moon sinks into it, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp nibbles its edge.

芋.meaning: A gardener sticks a <part>hat stand</part> in her vegetable patch as a scarecrow, and the crows just perch on it. But under the <part>grass</part> at its foot, something swells until it lifts the stand off the ground. She digs, and out comes a hairy brown root as big as a football: a giant <kanji>taro</kanji>.
芋.on: She slices it into a steaming bowl of hot <sound>u</sound>don.
芋.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeaks a mouse in the hole, waving a tiny <sound>mo</sound>p.

遍.meaning: A skater nails wheels to an old <part>notice board</part> and rides it down every <part>ramp</part> in the city, the flyers still pinned to it peeling off in the wind. By noon there are lost-parrot posters on rooftops, buses and one puzzled cow. They're <kanji>everywhere</kanji>.
遍.on: A <sound>hen</sound> pecks one off the pavement and wears it as a cape.
遍.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps a <sound>ma</sound>ma on a balcony as a flyer flutters into her butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t.

唯.meaning: At a bird choir contest, a hundred beaks open wide, but the judges creep along the rows and find that only one <part>mouth</part> is making a sound: a tiny <part>sparrow</part> at the back. The rest were miming. She takes the trophy, won <kanji>solely</kanji> by her own song.
唯.on: Her prize is a <sound>yu</sound>zu, which she shares with an <sound>ee</sound>l in the pond.
唯.kun: The mimers sulk on top of a <sound>ta</sound>co stand, and a <sound>du</sound>ck tells them they only have themselves to blame.

郊.meaning: The last bus stop is marked by a single <part>pennant</part> on a pole. Here bankers stepping off the bus <part>mingle</part> with goats chewing the timetable, and a tractor waits at the zebra crossing. Not quite town, not quite country: the <kanji>outskirts</kanji>.
郊.on: A goat swipes a banker's ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne and trots off into the fields.

累.meaning: Each day a scarecrow in the <part>rice field</part> ties one knot in a long <part>thread</part> to count the crows he has scared off. The thread coils round his post, trails across the paddy and wraps the farmhouse twice. The knots never stop: they <kanji>accumulate</kanji>.
累.on: In the end the thread drags down an old stone <sound>ru</sound>in at the edge of the field.
